Q: How to score content readability with multiple algorithms in Node.js CI pipeline? A:

You have to write your wrapper that addresses the issues you mention:

One algorithm isn't enough

There are already libraries for multiple evaluation (gunning fog and flesch).

No status labels

You have to make decisions about how to weight the output from the different tests and decide the final outcome accordingly.

HTML stripping

There are enough libraries doing that.

No composite result

See above, return true or false based on your needs.

No TypeScript types

The linked packages are fully typed. Just type your wrapper and you shall be done, good work!

Q: How to Define array values in YAML and fetch the keys - Mule 4 A:

I understand that you want to find the key in the input YAML for a given value. You can use the function findKeyForValue() below. It transverse the objects and arrays to find the value, then return the key to which value belongs. It may require changes for more complex structures.

%dw 2.0
output application/java
import * from dw::core::Arrays
fun findKeyForValue(x, v) = do {
    fun findKeyInternal(x,v,lastKeyName) =
        x match {
            case o is Object -> namesOf(o) flatMap findKeyInternal(o[$], v, $) filter $ != null
            case a is Array -> if (a some ($ == v)) lastKeyName else null
            else -> $
        }
    var result=findKeyInternal(x, v, "")
    ---
    if (sizeOf(result)>0) result[0] else null

}
---
findKeyForValue(vars.code, "emp2")

Output for the input in the question:

"employee"

Q: C/C++ : why variables in main() are on the stack? A:

If you want this array kept in .data area, the use keyword static like in your second example. But remember that in such case this variable will be shared for each call of given function. For that reason this is not a default behavior. Standard requires that each local variable is unique to each function call and its lifetime is associated with this function call. Using stack is cheapest way to achieve this. This is why compilers are doing that. Note that C/C++ standard do not define stack since not all hardware which can use C/C++ have this feature. This is why standard do not specify this only desired behavior.

In case of main this is safe since main can be called only once (calling main leads to Undefined Behavior).

Then you'd want to use IServiceScopeFactory, because you want to ensure the scope is being created, before anything is resolved.
